questions.stem: 提示：某高中調查學生每天花在手機、平板與電腦螢幕上的時間，並依用途分成課業、社群媒體、影音與遊戲四類，結果如下圖。請根據圖表內容，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段描述圖表的主要結果，並比較平日與假日的差異；第二段評估這樣的使用習慣對高中生的影響是否值得擔心，並提出一個具體可行的改善做法。

1.explanation_zh: 這一題有四個要求：第一段描述圖表並比較平日與假日；第二段先評估這樣的習慣是否值得擔心，再提出改善做法。第一段不必把八個數字全部念一遍，而是挑出 2–3 個對比：假日合計 8.7 小時、接近平日 4.8 小時的兩倍；影音增加最多；課業是唯一減少的用途。第二段只說「螢幕不好」而沒有說明影響，或做法空泛（例如「要有自制力」），內容分數會偏低。
evidence: 第一段描述圖表的主要結果，並比較平日與假日的差異
評估這樣的使用習慣對高中生的影響是否值得擔心
提出一個具體可行的改善做法
1.strategy_zh: 先決定立場（值得擔心或不必過度擔心），再用「多出來的時間從哪裡來」帶出影響；做法寫成能執行的步驟（設定上限、追蹤、學校活動）。
hints: 第一段：先寫總量（4.8 對 8.7），再寫增加最多與唯一減少的用途
第二段前半：表明立場，用一個因果鏈或自己的經驗說明影響
第二段後半：提出具體做法，承認螢幕也有好處，最後寫出自己的見解

content.focus_zh: 第一段要讀出 2–3 個明確對比（假日總時數接近平日兩倍、影音增加最多、只有課業減少），數字要和圖表一致；第二段要對「是否值得擔心」表明立場並說明影響，再提出具體可行的做法。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

checklist_zh: 第一段有沒有讀出 2–3 個明確對比（例如總時數、增加最多的用途、唯一減少的用途），而且數字和圖表一致
第二段有沒有清楚表明值不值得擔心，並用因果說明影響（多出來的時間是從哪裡擠出來的）
提出的做法是否具體可行：誰來做、做什麼、怎麼知道有沒有效
有沒有至少一個讓步或反面考量（例如螢幕也有好處），結尾是否提出自己的見解，而不是重述數字

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The chart shows how many hours students at one high school spend on screens every day. On weekdays, they use screens for 4.8 hours in total, and schoolwork takes up the largest part with 2.0 hours. On weekends, however, the total rises to 8.7 hours. The biggest change is in watching videos, which jumps from 1.0 hour to 2.8 hours. Time on social media and games also more than doubles. In contrast, schoolwork is the only use that drops, from 2.0 to 1.5 hours.
In my opinion, these numbers are worth worrying about. Spending almost nine hours a day on screens leaves little time for sleep, exercise, and real conversations. I know this from my own experience. Last semester, I often watched videos until two in the morning on weekends, so I felt tired and could not focus in class on Mondays. To solve this problem, students can set a daily time limit on their phones. For example, when I set a two-hour limit for video apps, my phone locked them after the time was up, and I started to read and jog more. In short, screens are useful tools, but we should control them instead of letting them control us.

self_assessment.explanation_zh: 兩段都回應題目：第一段讀出總量、增加最多與唯一減少三個對比，第二段有立場、經驗與做法（內容 4）；段落分工清楚，轉承語恰當但變化不多（組織 4）；句子正確，以簡單句和常見複句為主（文法句構 4）；用字正確但多是常用字，描述增減的動詞較少變化（字彙拼字 3）。總分 15，屬穩健版。

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
According to the survey, the screen habits of these high school students change dramatically once the school week ends. On weekdays, they spend an average of 4.8 hours a day in front of screens, and schoolwork accounts for the largest share at 2.0 hours. On weekends, by contrast, the total soars to 8.7 hours, almost twice the weekday figure. What drives this jump is entertainment rather than study. Video watching nearly triples, rising from 1.0 to 2.8 hours, while social media climbs from 1.2 to 2.5 hours and gaming from 0.6 to 1.9 hours. Schoolwork, meanwhile, is the only category that shrinks, falling to 1.5 hours. In other words, screens serve mainly as study tools from Monday to Friday but turn into recreational devices as soon as students have free time.
Although screens are not harmful in themselves, I believe the weekend pattern deserves attention, because those extra hours have to come from somewhere. Every additional hour of scrolling is usually an hour taken from sleep, exercise, or face-to-face time with family. I noticed this chain reaction in myself last semester. After staying up late watching short videos on Saturdays, I would wake up near noon, skip my usual basketball game, and then feel too tired to finish my homework on Sunday night. Admittedly, some online activities, such as chatting with friends, help teenagers stay connected, so banning screens would be neither realistic nor fair. A more practical solution is to plan screen time deliberately rather than simply cut it, since the real problem is not the device itself but the endless temptation of just one more video. For instance, students could set a weekend screen budget in advance, say three hours for entertainment, and track it with the time-limit function that most phones already have. Schools could also encourage this habit by holding a two-week challenge in which classes share their results. If teenagers learn to treat their attention as something valuable to spend wisely, they will gain not only more rest but also a stronger sense of autonomy over their own lives.

paragraphs.function_zh: 描述數據＋比較：先點出平日與假日的落差，再用倍數與增減說明娛樂用途是主因，最後歸納螢幕角色的轉變

errors.excerpt: screens serve mainly as study tools from Monday to Friday
errors.explanation_zh: 用字與圖表不符：平日課業只占 4.8 小時中的 2.0 小時，社群、影音、遊戲合計 2.8 小時，課業只是「最大的單一用途」，不是「主要」用途；mainly 的概括和第一段自己引用的數字矛盾。
errors.suggestion: In other words, schoolwork is the single biggest use of screens from Monday to Friday, but entertainment takes over as soon as students have free time.

top.comment_zh: 第一段數字全部正確，先總量再個別用途，triples、soars、climbs、shrinks 等動詞多變；第二段立場清楚，以「多出來的時間從哪裡來」說明影響，親身經驗具體，先讓步再提出「週末螢幕預算＋手機限時功能」的做法並延伸到學校，結尾有見解。唯一的問題是第一段結論句說平日螢幕「主要」用於課業，與圖表不符（平日課業 2.0 小時，娛樂三項合計 2.8 小時）。

steady.comment_zh: 回應了四項要求：總量、最大單項、影音增加最多、只有課業減少都讀得正確；第二段立場明確，熬夜看影片的經驗與設定使用時限的做法具體。句型以簡單句和並列句為主，複句不多；rises、jumps、more than doubles、drops 有變化，但 takes up the largest part with 2.0 hours 搭配略生硬。屬穩健、無錯誤但深度與句構變化較有限的文章。

steady.comment_zh: 兩段分工清楚，第一段列出總時數與各項對比，數字正確；第二段立場明確、有經驗、建議（設定使用時限）具體。句型以簡單句與合句為主，變化有限，用字正確但偏基本；『almost nine hours a day』其實只是假日的數字，略不精確。語言無誤。
